module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 1096

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/1096](https://www.erdosproblems.com/1096)
- [ErKo98] Erdős, P. and Komornik, V., Developments in non-integer bases.
  Acta Math. Hungar. (1998), 57--83.
- [Fe16] Feng, D.-J., On the topology of polynomials with bounded integer coefficients.
  J. Eur. Math. Soc. (2016), 181--193.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Filter
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos1096

/--
Let $1<q<1+\epsilon$ and consider the set of numbers of the shape
$\sum_{i\in S}q^i$ (for all finite $S$), ordered by size as
$0=x_1<x_2<\cdots$.

Is it true that, provided $\epsilon>0$ is sufficiently small, $x_{k+1}-x_k \to 0$?

This was solved affirmatively by Erdős and Komornik [ErKo98], who proved the conclusion
whenever $1<q<\sqrt{q_1}$, where $q_1$ is the second Pisot-Vijayaraghavan number.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11,
  formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/dfe2d78128b493c572cf525b1b8edf4897fb7664/src/latest/ErdosProblems/Erdos1096.lean#L44"]
theorem erdos_1096 :
    answer(True) ↔ ∃ ε > 0, ∀ q, 1 < q → q < 1 + ε →
    ∀ x : ℕ → ℝ, StrictMono x → Set.range x = { ∑ i ∈ S, q ^ i | S : Finset ℕ } →
    Tendsto (fun k => x (k + 1) - x k) atTop (𝓝 0) := by
  sorry

-- TODO: add variants and additional material from the Erdős Problems page.

end Erdos1096

reformulations.difference: The source names the increasing enumeration of the power-sum set. Lean instead quantifies over every strictly increasing sequence with exactly that range, without separately asserting existence or specifying its initial value.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For every real q > 1, the set contains 0 and all q^n, hence is infinite and unbounded. Every bounded initial segment is finite: if q^N > B, any power sum at most B has support contained in {0,…,N−1}. Consequently the set has a unique increasing enumeration indexed by ℕ, whose initial value is necessarily 0. Universal quantification over such enumerations therefore states the property of the source's ordered sequence, not a vacuous implication. In /workspace/review/scratch.lean, I proved finite sublevels, enumeration existence and uniqueness, the initial value, and the full ε/q-scoped equivalence with an existential enumeration starting at 0. These proofs use only standard axioms.

Current status was independently checked in the source-linked database: informal status 'proved' (2026-04-24), formal status 'Lean' (2026-08-23). The exact linked external theorem and its five dependencies were compiled together in /workspace/review/external-proof-combined.lean; #print axioms reports only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound.
